recognized_transcript: A report returned zero rows. Without receipts, Decider picked Inspect Pipeline on three calls.
Each spent its one red and ended unresolved. Decider serves from a private, always on Amazon Sage
Maker Endpoint. Amazon Bedrock Novolite narrates only after completion. Offline, we ran every
diagnostic and trained low RA plus Decider's Choice Head on Verifier Labels. At runtime,
the receipt removes one repeat, low RA ranks what remains, the Verifier owns truth,
The reusable recipe sends current state and matching history to Decider.
Only a proven exact repeat is withheld before selection. A receipt cannot pick a tool. Decider
chooses from the remaining tools. Run one happens once, one inference, 21.6 seconds of client time,
one read, unresolved. The deterministic Verifier stored a decision receipt, real data, no decision
moved. The model is unchanged. The system recorded a fact. Run two is a new call,
and the exact receipt matches. Before the first Decider request and before any read,
the controller precludes only the proven dead end. Decider makes one fresh choice,
inspects schema keys. One inference, one read, a verified repair, completed in 26.6 seconds.
Old Run 2 took 54.8 seconds and two inferences. Optimized Run 2 takes 26.6 seconds and one inference.
That is one fewer inference and an observed difference of 28.2 seconds or 51.4% lower client latency.
One synthetic case, each proof once. Across 160 decisions, correct first
choices rose from 97 to 129. Across 64 calls, wasted first reads fell from 20 to 15 and completions
rose from 44 to 49. CPU replay confirmed direction, one seed, experimental checkpoint.
One failed decision becomes a boundary. History can rule out one proven execution under one
identical context. It cannot choose the next tool. Decider chooses. The Verifier decides what the read
found.
